question.text: Where do traffic signals control vehicles and pedestrians?

answer.text: Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and at some mid-block crosswalks.

teaching.text: Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and mid-block crosswalks. Remember: intersections and mid-block crosswalks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and at some mid-block crosswalks.

question.text: What does a circular green light allow, and what must turning drivers do?

answer.text: A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

teaching.text: On a circular green you may go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Remember: green go, turners yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question.text: What should you do at a circular yellow light?

answer.text: A circular yellow light warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through.

teaching.text: A circular yellow warns red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely. Remember: stop unless too close.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A circular yellow light warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through.

question.text: Should you speed up on a yellow light to beat the red?

answer.text: Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red.

teaching.text: Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before red. Remember: never race the yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red.

question.text: What does a steady circular red mean, and when may you turn right?

answer.text: A steady circular red means stop, and you may then turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.

teaching.text: A steady circular red means stop, then you may turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted. Remember: stop, then right on red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady circular red means stop, and you may then turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.

question.text: Whom must you yield to when turning right on red?

answer.text: A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic.

teaching.text: Turning right on red, yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in or starting to cross the intersection. Remember: yield to walkers and traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic.

question.text: What is the penalty for failing to yield to a pedestrian while turning right on red?

answer.text: Failing to yield to such a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a penalty of at least one hundred dollars and no more than five hundred dollars.

teaching.text: Failing to yield to that pedestrian on right on red carries a penalty of one hundred to five hundred dollars. Remember: fines for not yielding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to yield to such a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a penalty of at least one hundred dollars and no more than five hundred dollars.

question.text: What does a green arrow give you?

answer.text: A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points.

teaching.text: A green arrow gives a protected movement; enter carefully in the direction it points. Remember: green arrow, protected turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points.

question.text: How does turning on a circular green differ from turning on a green arrow?

answer.text: A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn.

teaching.text: A circular green turn must yield first, while a green arrow gives a protected turn. Remember: circle yields, arrow protected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn.

question.text: When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows, who yields?

answer.text: When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver.

teaching.text: When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows, the U-turning driver yields. Remember: U-turn yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver.

question.text: What does a red arrow mean?

answer.text: A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop.

teaching.text: A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop. Remember: red arrow, no turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop.

question.text: How does a circular red differ from a red arrow for turning?

answer.text: A steady circular red still allows a right turn after a full stop unless signed otherwise, while a red arrow stops all turning traffic in that direction.

teaching.text: A steady circular red still allows a right after a full stop unless signed, while a red arrow stops that turn. Remember: circle allows right, arrow stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady circular red still allows a right turn after a full stop unless signed otherwise, while a red arrow stops all turning traffic in that direction.

question.text: What does a yellow arrow warn you about?

answer.text: A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow.

teaching.text: A yellow arrow warns the protected green arrow is ending. Remember: protected phase ending.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow.

question.text: How does a circular yellow differ from a yellow arrow?

answer.text: A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end.

teaching.text: A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected phase is ending. Remember: circle warns red, arrow ends.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end.

question.text: When no arrow is lit on a combined signal, what controls turning traffic?

answer.text: Some signals combine protected arrows with unprotected circular lights; when no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic.

teaching.text: When no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic. Remember: no arrow, circles rule.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some signals combine protected arrows with unprotected circular lights; when no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic.

question.text: When arrows and circular lights show together, which controls turns?

answer.text: When arrows and circular lights show together, the arrows control turning traffic and the circular lights control through traffic.

teaching.text: When arrows and circular lights show together, arrows control turns and circles control through traffic. Remember: arrows turn, circles through.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When arrows and circular lights show together, the arrows control turning traffic and the circular lights control through traffic.

question.text: How should you treat an intersection whose signal is dark or malfunctioning?

answer.text: At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign.

teaching.text: Treat a dark or malfunctioning signal as if every approach had a stop sign. Remember: dark signal, all-way stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign.

question.text: When does the all-way stop rule for a broken signal not apply?

answer.text: The all-way-stop rule for a broken signal does not apply when an officer or other authorized person directs traffic or another control device is working.

teaching.text: That all-way-stop rule does not apply when an officer directs traffic or another control device is working. Remember: officer or device overrides.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The all-way-stop rule for a broken signal does not apply when an officer or other authorized person directs traffic or another control device is working.

question.text: What do you do at a dark signal, and what overrides that rule?

answer.text: A dark or broken traffic signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working.

teaching.text: A dark signal is an all-way stop, unless an officer or another working device controls traffic. Remember: stop all ways, unless directed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A dark or broken traffic signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working.

question.text: What does a flashing red light mean?

answer.text: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop and wait until you can enter without interfering with approaching traffic.

teaching.text: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Remember: flashing red is stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop and wait until you can enter without interfering with approaching traffic.

question.text: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

answer.text: A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution. Remember: flashing yellow is caution.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution.

question.text: How does a flashing red differ from a flashing yellow?

answer.text: A flashing red works like a stop sign and a flashing yellow works like a warning sign.

teaching.text: Flashing red works like a stop sign, and flashing yellow works like a warning sign. Remember: red stops, yellow slows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing red works like a stop sign and a flashing yellow works like a warning sign.

question.text: What does a flashing yellow arrow permit, and what must you do first?

answer.text: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn shown, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Remember: turn after yielding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn shown, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question.text: On a flashing yellow arrow head, what do solid red and solid yellow arrows mean?

answer.text: On a flashing yellow arrow signal head, a solid red arrow means stop with no turn allowed, and a solid yellow arrow means get ready to stop.

teaching.text: On a flashing yellow arrow head, a solid red arrow means stop and a solid yellow arrow means get ready to stop. Remember: solid red stop, yellow prepare.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a flashing yellow arrow signal head, a solid red arrow means stop with no turn allowed, and a solid yellow arrow means get ready to stop.

question.text: How does a flashing yellow arrow differ from a solid yellow arrow?

answer.text: A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding, while a solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding, while a solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop. Remember: flashing turns, solid prepares.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding, while a solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop.

question.text: What does a solid green arrow mean on a flashing yellow arrow head?

answer.text: A solid green arrow on that head allows the turn without yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, though you still proceed with caution.

teaching.text: A solid green arrow on that head allows the turn without yielding, still with caution. Remember: solid green, no yielding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid green arrow on that head allows the turn without yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, though you still proceed with caution.

question.text: What may a right-turn signal head show instead of a red arrow?

answer.text: Signal heads for right turns may show a steady circular red instead of a red arrow.

teaching.text: Right-turn signal heads may show a steady circular red instead of a red arrow. Remember: circular red for rights.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signal heads for right turns may show a steady circular red instead of a red arrow.

question.text: What does a ramp meter control?

answer.text: A ramp meter controls traffic entering a freeway from an interchange entrance ramp.

teaching.text: A ramp meter controls traffic entering a freeway from an interchange entrance ramp. Remember: meters control ramp entry.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A ramp meter controls traffic entering a freeway from an interchange entrance ramp.

question.text: What do red and green mean at a ramp meter?

answer.text: At a ramp meter, steady red means stop and wait, and steady green means go down the ramp and merge onto the freeway.

teaching.text: At a ramp meter, steady red means stop and wait, and steady green means go and merge. Remember: red waits, green merges.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a ramp meter, steady red means stop and wait, and steady green means go down the ramp and merge onto the freeway.

question.text: What may you do when a ramp meter is dark?

answer.text: If a ramp meter is dark, showing neither red nor green, you may continue without stopping and merge or yield as conditions allow.

teaching.text: If a ramp meter is dark, you may continue without stopping and merge or yield as conditions allow. Remember: dark meter, merge on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a ramp meter is dark, showing neither red nor green, you may continue without stopping and merge or yield as conditions allow.

question.text: How does a red ramp meter differ from a dark one?

answer.text: A ramp meter showing red means stop and wait, but a ramp meter showing nothing at all means you may merge without stopping.

teaching.text: A red ramp meter means stop and wait, but a dark one means you may merge without stopping. Remember: red stops, dark goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A ramp meter showing red means stop and wait, but a ramp meter showing nothing at all means you may merge without stopping.

question.text: Where are hybrid beacons used, and what do they show before activation?

answer.text: Hybrid beacons can control traffic at mid-block crosswalks and at the entrances of emergency response facilities, and stay dark until a pedestrian or responder activates them.

teaching.text: Hybrid beacons control mid-block crosswalks and emergency facility entrances, staying dark until activated. Remember: dark until activated.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hybrid beacons can control traffic at mid-block crosswalks and at the entrances of emergency response facilities, and stay dark until a pedestrian or responder activates them.

question.text: What sequence does a hybrid beacon show once activated?

answer.text: Once activated, a hybrid beacon flashes yellow, then shows steady yellow and then steady red so moving vehicles can stop safely.

teaching.text: Once activated, a hybrid beacon flashes yellow, then shows steady yellow, then steady red. Remember: flash yellow, yellow, red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once activated, a hybrid beacon flashes yellow, then shows steady yellow and then steady red so moving vehicles can stop safely.

question.text: What do vehicles do while a hybrid beacon shows steady red?

answer.text: While a hybrid beacon shows steady red, vehicles stay stopped as pedestrians cross or emergency vehicles leave their station.

teaching.text: While a hybrid beacon shows steady red, vehicles stay stopped. Remember: steady red, stay stopped.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While a hybrid beacon shows steady red, vehicles stay stopped as pedestrians cross or emergency vehicles leave their station.

question.text: When may you go at a hybrid beacon showing flashing red?

answer.text: When the hybrid beacon switches to flashing red, stay stopped until the pedestrians or emergency vehicles have cleared; then, after a full stop, you may proceed while it still flashes.

teaching.text: On flashing red, stay stopped until the crossing clears, then go after a full stop. Remember: clear, stop, then go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the hybrid beacon switches to flashing red, stay stopped until the pedestrians or emergency vehicles have cleared; then, after a full stop, you may proceed while it still flashes.

question.text: How does a beacon's steady red differ from its flashing red?

answer.text: At a hybrid beacon, steady red means stay stopped, while flashing red lets you go after a full stop once the crossing is clear.

teaching.text: Steady red at a beacon means stay stopped, while flashing red lets you go after a full stop once clear. Remember: steady stays, flashing may go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a hybrid beacon, steady red means stay stopped, while flashing red lets you go after a full stop once the crossing is clear.

question.text: What does a hybrid beacon do after its cycle?

answer.text: After its cycle, a hybrid beacon goes dark again until the next activation.

teaching.text: After its cycle, a hybrid beacon goes dark again until the next activation. Remember: back to dark.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After its cycle, a hybrid beacon goes dark again until the next activation.

question.text: How does a hybrid beacon's sequence differ from a ramp meter's displays?

answer.text: A hybrid beacon begins with flashing yellow and then steady yellow before red, unlike a ramp meter that shows only red or green.

teaching.text: A hybrid beacon shows yellow phases before red, unlike a ramp meter that shows only red or green. Remember: beacon yellows first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A hybrid beacon begins with flashing yellow and then steady yellow before red, unlike a ramp meter that shows only red or green.

hooks_spoken: Circular green means go, with turners yielding; yellow means stop unless too close.
Steady red means stop, then right on red unless signed, yielding to walkers.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of circular signals. Circular green means go, with turners yielding; yellow means stop unless too close. Steady red means stop, then right on red unless signed, yielding to walkers. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A green arrow is a protected turn; a circular green turn must yield.
A red arrow stops turns; a circular red still allows a right after stopping.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of arrow signals. A green arrow is a protected turn; a circular green turn must yield. A red arrow stops turns; a circular red still allows a right after stopping. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A dark signal is an all-way stop unless an officer directs traffic.
Flashing red means stop; flashing yellow means caution.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of dark and flashing signals. A dark signal is an all-way stop unless an officer directs traffic. Flashing red means stop; flashing yellow means caution. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding.
A solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of flashing yellow arrow signals. A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding. A solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Ramp meter red means wait, green means merge.
A dark ramp meter means merge without stopping.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of ramp meters. Ramp meter red means wait, green means merge. A dark ramp meter means merge without stopping. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A hybrid beacon flashes yellow, shows yellow, then red.
Steady red stay stopped; flashing red, stop then go when clear.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of hybrid beacons. A hybrid beacon flashes yellow, shows yellow, then red. Steady red stay stopped; flashing red, stop then go when clear. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
